html:
On 17 July 1998 an earthquake off the north coast of Papua New Guinea set off a tsunami that struck villages near Aitape. More than 2,000 people died.

The waves were far larger than such an earthquake should have made. Scientists later found that the quake had set off an undersea landslide, which raised the water. This changed how tsunami risks are judged worldwide.

Villages on a narrow sandbar between the sea and a lagoon were wiped out, and survivors were moved inland. Like the 2004 tsunami later, it pushed for warning systems around the Pacific. See also Papua New Guinea and tsunami.
